newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares notch up losses in end-account trade.
newsitem.headline: India shares notch up losses in end-account trade.

text.p: ** (1200 GMT) Squaring up of deals on last day of weekly
account at Bombay exchange drags down prices
** Bombay's benchmark index ends near day's lows at
3,870.26, falls 64.95 pts, or 1.65 pct
** Market rumours about Congress party opposing amnesty
scheme and large tax cuts proposed in govt's 1997/98
budget plays on minds of operators
** Delhi index falls 0.93 pts to 828.33, Calcutta gains
0.92 pts to 475.57 and Madras up 56.57 pts to 3,764.83
** Carry-forward charges expected to rise sharply this week
indicating huge overbought position, say dealers
Indian shares ended a week dominated by post-budget cheer on a predictable down note on Thursday as traders closed out positions for the end of the account period, dealers said.
Markets are closed on Friday for a religious holiday.

Rumours that the Congress party, which backs the ruling coalition, will oppose some government measures presented in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget last week also put pressure on prices, dealers said.
Declines were concentrated in benchmark stocks, but traders noted some funds buying to take advantage of the price dips.
"These (Congress party) reports have led to some selling in the market," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Bombay's Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.
He said sharp price differences at the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) indicated huge arbitrage opportunities.
Late on Thursday, the Congress criticised the budget, but said the party had not taken a final stand on it.
Expectations of higher carry-forward charges of 4-5 percent a month compared to 2-3 percent a week ago adding to the selling pressure, some traders said.
The carry-forward charges will be fixed on Saturday.
Higher rates reflect huge overbought positions.
Foreign funds were however picking up pivotals at lower levels, traders said. "There is no panic in the market," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities.
"There has been a lot of buying in blue chips such as MTNL, TELCO, Mahindra & Mahindra and HPCL," he added.
The Bombay index hit 4,029.56 this week against 3,474.79 in pre-budget trade after the budget proposed sharp cuts in corporate and personal taxes.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
